plugin_platform_handler.probe: PluginContext has register_platform_handler and spawn_task; the Telegram adapter calls _wire_plugin_handlers(app) from connect()
plugin_platform_handler.contract: ctx.register_platform_handler('telegram', factory) -> factory(native, adapter) at every connect(), including reconnects with a NEW adapter instance; ctx.spawn_task(coro) supervised, cancelled on unload; adapter.send/edit_message return SendResult; edit_message does NOT forward to the replacement adapter, so the live adapter is re-resolved per tick via adapter.gateway_runner.adapters and only used when is_connected; edit_message(chat, id, text) without finalize sends PLAIN text (no parse_mode; the PTB Application is built without Defaults) and truncates an over-long payload in place, while finalize=True converts to MarkdownV2 and splits an over-long escaped payload into NEW continuation messages, so the dashboard never edits with finalize; a parse mode is not reachable through the public verb, the adapter's own _edit_text takes one (row screen_html), and the plain public edit stays the fallback

plugin_platform_handler.caveat: user plugins are opt-in: the plugin key must be listed in plugins.enabled (hermes_cli/plugins_discovery.py gate_manifest), and the factory fires before the Bot is initialised, so the first tick waits for is_connected
plugin_platform_handler.deployment: the engine imports a directory plugin as package hermes_plugins.<slug> with __path__ = the plugin dir (hermes_cli/plugins_loader.py _load_directory_module), so telegram_dashboard/ copied INTO the plugin folder resolves as a relative package; verified through the real PluginManager.discover_and_load in tests/test_probe_plugin.py

screen_html.probe: the live adapter has a coroutine _edit_text; every tick calls _edit_text(chat, message_id, html, 'HTML') and, on any exception other than 'not modified', edits plain through the public edit_message in the same tick. Plain succeeded right after HTML failed = the HTML form was refused: screen_format 'plain' and the exception class in the record, HTML tried again after HTML_RETRY_TICKS (12). No _edit_text at all = plain, html_error 'no _edit_text'
screen_html.contract: TelegramAdapter._edit_text(self, chat_id: str, message_id: str, text: str, parse_mode: Any = None) -> None: normalizes the ids, passes parse_mode to Bot.edit_message_text only when given, raises the PTB error on refusal ('Message is not modified' included). A PRIVATE method: the plugin treats it as a capability, never as a promise, and the public plain edit is always the fallback. The parse mode is the string 'HTML' (ParseMode.HTML is that string); the markup is <b> and one <blockquote expandable>, both Bot API 7.4+, not the rich_message parameter

hermes_version.probe: sys.modules['hermes_cli'].__version__ is a non-empty string: the module the gateway imported at start-up, looked up, never imported; absent = the line says no data (not on this installation). Never importlib.metadata (an editable install keeps the dist-info of install time), never hermes_cli.build_info.get_code_identity(refresh=True) (it would restamp the running gateway's code_sha)
hermes_version.contract: GET https://api.github.com/repos/NousResearch/hermes-agent/releases/latest and /releases?per_page=100, no token, at most once a day (release_cache in the plugin record, failures cached too), in the plugin's own worker under a 25 s deadline; version from the release name 'Hermes Agent vX.Y.Z (...)', releases behind = position on the list (drafts and pre-releases skipped), never arithmetic on version numbers. Observed without a token on 2026-09-25: 36 releases, every name in that form, newest first. Not a source: moves neither the status nor the coverage. The engine's banner.check_for_updates (commits behind main) is not used
